frames.narration: An engineer submits a production job: 50 tasks, each with a CPU and memory limit, a priority in the production band and a few constraints. The request goes to the elected Borgmaster, which first checks that the engineer has enough quota at that priority. Without it the job is rejected on the spot.
The job is written to the Paxos store on a majority of the five Borgmaster replicas, and its tasks go into the pending queue. From here the cell state survives the loss of a replica.

messages.label: record the job, add tasks to the pending queue

frames.narration: The scheduler works on a cached copy of the cell state. It scans the pending queue from high to low priority. For one task per group of identical tasks it does feasibility checking, which machines have room, counting room held by lower-priority tasks as available, and then scores the feasible machines, looking at them in random order until it has enough.

The scheduler picks machine A, which scores best (fewest stranded resources, packages already installed) but needs a batch task preempted. It tells the master. The master checks the assignment against its current state and accepts it, in the spirit of optimistic concurrency control.

messages.label: assign task to A, evicting a batch task

frames.narration: The Borgmaster tells Machine A's Borglet to start the task. The Borglet installs the packages, which takes most of the typical 25 seconds of startup, kills the preempted batch task, and starts the new task. The batch task goes back to the pending queue.

messages.label: start the task, stop the batch task

frames.narration: Later Machine A stops answering the master's polls. After several missed polls the master marks it down and reschedules its tasks, here onto Machine B. If Machine A returns, the master tells it to kill the tasks that were moved. The tasks on Machine B keep running even if the Borgmaster itself were to fail.

Meanwhile the Borglets report usage every few seconds. The master computes a reservation for each task, which decays from its limit towards its real usage plus a safety margin. What is left over is lent to batch tasks, and if a machine runs short the batch tasks are killed or throttled, never the production ones.

states.master: reservation below limit; the rest lent to batch work
